title: Electromyometrial Imaging of Uterine Contractions in Pregnant Women
protocol: Print MRI and electrode patch templates on paper.
Cut clear vinyl sheets into 22 rectangular patches measuring 120 mm x 60 mm.
Cut silicone rubber sheets into 44 rectangular patches measuring 120 mm x 60 mm.
Cut clear vinyl sheets into 4 square patches measuring 60 mm x 60 mm.
Cut silicone rubber sheets into 8 square patches measuring 60 mm x 60 mm.
Overlay a template with a clear vinyl patch.
Glue MRI-safe markers to the vinyl patch at the centers of the circles representing electrode holder cavities.
Label circle locations on the silicone rubber patches.
Punch holes at labeled locations using an 8 mm diameter punch set.
Attach electrode holders over each hole using double-sided adhesive collars.
Align the circumference of the electrode holder cavity with the circumference of the punched hole.
Install the X-ring into the cavity on top of the electrode holder.
Cover the holder with the color-coded silicone sheet.
Insert the pin-type active electrode through the X-ring into the holder.
Center the electrode in the cavity of the electrode holder.
Place the electrode cables between the two layers of silicone sheets and along the long edge.
Adjust the length of the electrode cable by twining it around the electrode holder if needed.
Apply three strips of medical-grade double-sided tape to the electrode patch between the rows of electrodes along the long edge of the patch.
Cut six measuring tapes at their 30 cm marks.
Retain the top section from 0 cm to 30 cm for each tape.
Glue the edges at 0 cm of two measuring tapes to a long piece of vinyl strip with a gap in the width of the tape.
Apply double-sided adhesive tape to each ruler.
Store the patches and rulers in a closed-lid storage box.
Ask the subject to change into MR-safe pants and gown provided by the MRI technician.
Place MR-safe marker patches on the back surface in the exam room.
Instruct the subject to sit on a medical exam bed.
Apply a vertical ruler along the subject's spine, with the end of the ruler at the buttock cleavage.
Place a horizontal ruler at the level of the iliac crest, centered over the vertical ruler.
Peel the liner off the double-sided tape on the patches and apply two rectangular patches on the back.
Position the long edges of the patches next to the vertical ruler with corners at the intersection of both rulers.
Apply additional patches bilaterally symmetric to the first two patches for average-sized subjects, placing four patches at each side.
Place MR-safe marker patches on the abdominal surface.
Raise the head of the exam bed to around 40° and guide the subject to lie down in Fowler's position.
Place a vertical ruler along the midline of the abdomen with the 3 cm mark near the fundus region determined by manual palpation.
Apply a horizontal ruler so that its center is at the 6 cm mark of the vertical ruler, extending left and right along the natural curvature of the abdomen.
Place the first rectangular patch above the horizontal ruler and to the left of the vertical ruler.
Align one corner of the first patch with the intersection of the two rulers.
Place the second rectangular patch to the left of the first patch along the horizontal ruler.
Position the third and fourth patches directly below the horizontal ruler, vertically aligned with the first and second patches.
Place the fifth rectangular patch below the third patch, aligning its short edge along the vertical ruler.
Place the sixth rectangular patch next to the fifth patch on the left side.
Position the seventh patch below the fifth patch, aligning its short edge along the vertical ruler.
Leave gaps of 2-3 cm between patches 3, 5, and 7 for the curvature of the abdomen.
Place square patches s1 and s2 vertically aligned with the sixth and seventh patches respectively.
Ensure patches on the right abdominal surface are bilaterally symmetric to those on the left.
Take photos and notes of the patch layout to record positions relative to rulers and umbilicus.
Screen the subject according to MRI safety rules at Zone II of the MRI facility.
Guide the subject through Zone III to Zone IV where a 3 T MR scanner resides.
Guide the patient to lie down on the MRI bed in a supine position.
Provide the patient with an MR-safe microphone.
Give the patient a headphone set.
Offer the patient a signaling squeeze ball.
Cover the subject's lower abdomen with a 32-array MRI coil.
Adjust the field of view using the localizer to cover the entire uterus and cervix.
Perform an MRI scan with a T1-weighted sequence using volume-interpolated breath-hold examination.
Store the MR images in DICOM format.
Remove the MRI patches and rulers from the subject.
Clean the patient's abdomen and back with baby wipes.
Disinfect the patches with germicidal disposable wipes.
Apply new double-sided tape for the next experiment.
Prepare the electrode patches by filling conductive gel into a curved tip irrigation syringe.
Add the gel into the electrode holder cavities on each electrode patch using the syringe.
Remove the liners of the double-sided tapes on the electrode patches.
Apply the electrode patches according to the placement layout described in the photos and notes taken previously.
Connect the power and data cords of the 3D optical scanner.
Open the 3D scanning software.
Hold the handheld optical scanner upright, with the flashing cameras facing the subject.
Press the Start button on the scanner to start the scanning session.
Press the Start button again to begin recording the scanning process.
Move the scanner around the subject to capture 3D optical scans of electrode locations.
Take photos and notes of the patch layout.
Note the positions of the rulers relative to each other and the subject's navel.
Place the "LL" grounding electrode on the lower left abdomen.
Place the "LA" grounding electrode on the left upper chest.
Place the "RA" grounding electrode on the right upper chest.
Place the "DRL" grounding electrode on the abdominal surface near the umbilicus or the lower right abdomen.

Connect the components of the bioelectricity mapping hardware, including the laptop, analog to digital (AD) box, battery box, electrode patch, grounding electrode cables, optical fiber, and USB2 receiver.
Open the software Active View on the laptop and turn on the AD box.
Check the status light on the AD box. If it is yellow, remove the grounding electrodes, add more gel, and place them back in their locations until the status light turns blue.

Check the Electrode offset module in Active View. If any electrode has a large offset (over a quarter of the largest offset), secure the electrode with medical paper tapes or reinstall it by removing it, adding more gel, and placing it back.
Click Start file > Paused to save the bioelectricity signal data streams in real time.
Record for 900 seconds, then click Pause Save > Stop to finish the recording and store the multi-electrode measurement in a binary data file (BDF) file.
Repeat step 3.9 four times after ensuring the subject is comfortable and willing to continue.
Turn off the AD box after the last recording.
Disconnect the electrode patches, grounding electrodes, optical fiber, and USB cable.
Remove the electrode patches and grounding electrodes from the subject.
Clean the subject's abdomen and lower back with a towel or baby wipes.
Pack up all the equipment.
Store the electrode patches and grounding electrodes for cleaning.
Clean the electrode patches and grounding electrodes in lukewarm water with dish soap in the cleaning room.
Disinfect them with germicidal wipes.
Air-dry the patches.
Apply double-sided mounting tape to the patches and rulers for the next experiment.
Launch the data analysis software and load the MRI DICOM data.
Go to the Segmentation module and click New to create a new label.
Click Edit > Adjust the range to > Data histogram to change the image contrast.
In Sagittal View, choose the Brush tool, label the uterus boundaries of the MR images, fill in the regions, and add to the label file.
Repeat this step every three to five slices.
Select the segmented regions and click Selection > Interpolate > + to interpolate the segmentation of all the slices.
Click New to create a new label file.
Choose the Magic wand tool and place the masking threshold at the initial local minimum of the data histogram.
Adjust the threshold until the entire body is highlighted in blue.
Choose All slices, click on any blue region, and then click + to add the segmentation into the label file.
Click Segmentation > Fill holes > All slices > + to fix the holes.
Go to the Segmentation module and click New to create a new label for the uterus.
Manually segment the uterus on the MR images.
Use Interpolate if needed.
In the Project module, generate the surface data from the label files of the uterus and body surface.
Choose a surface file, reduce the number of faces in Simplification Editor > Simplify by 50%, and click Simplify now.
Choose the simplified surface file and right-click Smooth Surface (iteration = 20, lambda = 0.6) > Apply.
Then, choose the smoothed surface file and right-click Remesh Surface (% 100) > Apply to re-mesh each surface.
Continue performing these steps until the body surface comprises approximately 18,000 faces and the uterine surface comprises roughly 640 faces.
Click File > Export Data As > STL ascii to save the two surfaces in stereolithography (STL) format.
Choose the scan quality (geometry, texture), object size, hole-filling method (watertight) in the Model creation module.
Click Next.
Choose Lasso selection and erase redundant regions in the Editor module.
Click Next to create an automatic refinement of the scan.
Click Editor > Lasso selection to remove unnecessary regions.
Click File > Export Meshes > STL File Format to save the surface in STL format.
Align the optical 3D scan data to the MRI body surface using pre-programmed data analysis software.
Load the STL format surfaces generated from steps 4.1 and 4.2 with the data analysis software project.
Run the prompt TCL command line to prepare data analysis software objects for rigid alignment for the abdominal surface.
Click Two Viewers (horizontal) and display the optical scan torso surface in the left viewer and the MRI body surface in the right viewer.
Place five or six landmarks on both surfaces.
Run the prompt TCL command line to apply the rigid alignment.
Repeat steps 4.3.2-4.3.4 for the back surface.
Click Single Viewer and display the rigid-aligned optical-scanned body surface in the viewer.
Run the prompt TCL command line to prepare data analysis software objects for non-rigid alignment.
Click Project > Create Object > Landmarks and add landmarks at the electrode locations on the optical scanned body surface.
Export landmark files for non-rigid alignment using File > Export Data As > LandmarkSet Ascii.
Run the Geometry module in the EMMI data processing pipeline to perform a non-rigid alignment.
Import automatically aligned electrode landmarks and improve precision based on notes and photos from steps 2.3 and 3.3.
Export landmark files for electrode locations using File > Export Data As > LandmarkSet Ascii.
Load STL files and LandmarkSet files in the EMMI data processing pipeline-geometry module to generate body-uterus geometry in MAT format.
Run the EMMI data processing pipeline-EMG preprocessing module to load BDF file.
Process raw electrical signal with a Butterworth filter with frequency band 0.34-1 Hz.
Detect local and global artifacts in filtered signal using the EMMI data processing pipeline-artifacts detection module.
Load body-uterus geometry and preprocessed electrical signal data into the reconstruction module of the EMMI data processing pipeline.
Compute electrical signals on the uterine surface.
Run the EMMI data processing pipeline-EMG signal analysis module to automatically detect the onsets and offsets of each EMG burst on the uterine surface.
Choose the observation window on the cluster figure overlay.
Compute the activation time at each uterine location for every observation window.
Create an isochrone for each observation window.
